thread:
incident-bot: Incident alert: cont-batching-runner in us-west-2 reporting sustained error-rate increase + KV cache memory growth for model redwood/open-13b-q (service: cont-batch-v2). severity: P1. Auto-pager: paging to disk started. sample: 8% 5xx, 99p latency 2.7s -> baseline 180ms. Trigger: kvcache_total_bytes spike.

maya.k: ack. I’m on-call. pulling logs now. tagging raj and priya. @raj.r @priya.s can you join?

maya.k: quick note to cs: @cs-bot please flag top 5 customers with >1% error rate over last 10m for this model.

cs-bot: Noted. Top affected customers: AcmeHealth (3.6% errors), Vaultly (2.1%), EduForge (1.8%). All in us-west-2.

raj.r: saw the alert. jumping in. initial glance: cont-batch config for this fleet has max_num_seqs=512 and max_batch_tokens=32768 in the new rollout. I'm seeing a queue of partial batches holding KV slots; KVCACHE usage jumped from ~45GB to ~420GB in 6m. eviction thrash observed.

priya.s: logs show lots of retry loops due to timeouts: 
```
2026-03-15T09:12:34Z ERROR serve: request timeout after 10s for request_id=abc123 model=redwood/open-13b-q node=gpu-12
2026-03-15T09:12:36Z WARN kvcache: eviction miss loop triggered, freed 0 bytes
```

maya.k: hypothesis: continuous-batching misconfig (max_num_seqs too high) + a model variant with larger KV sizes caused KVCACHE blowup and paging, which then increased tail latency and triggered timeouts -> retries -> thrash.

tomas.v: confirm model variant opened yesterday has slightly larger per-token KV footprint (layer normalization change). Should have been in the model profile but wasn't. That plus 512 concurrent seqs is bad.

maya.k: immediate mitigation options: 1) roll back cont-batch config to previous safe values (max_num_seqs=128, max_batch_tokens=16384) 2) temporarily disable continuous batching for this model fleet 3) increase KVCACHE eviction aggressiveness and set hard cap. Which is fastest?

raj.r: fastest is to adjust config via runtime feature flag (we can push a per-fleet override). I can push a per-fleet max_num_seqs=64 and max_batch_tokens=8192 as a temporary throttle. That should free KV pressure quickly.

priya.s: disabling cont-batch whole fleet is riskier for throughput but would stop the thrash immediately. prefer targeted config override.

maya.k: go for targeted override. @raj.r please run the override and post the command. plan a canary to 10% of nodes then 100% if green.

raj.r: executing override now. command: `infractl runtime config set --fleet cont-batch-v2 --model redwood/open-13b-q --max_num_seqs 64 --max_batch_tokens 8192 --scope canary=10%`

deploy-bot: rollout started: cont-batch-v2 override -> redwood/open-13b-q canary=10% (nodes: 4/40).

maya.k: watching KPIs. priya, can you monitor KVCACHE total and eviction rates? tomas, monitor per-request KV size sample distribution. cs-bot keep customer hits updated.

priya.s: metrics: after override started, KVCACHE growth rate slowed. pre-override: +60GB/5m, now +6GB/5m. eviction misses down from 120/s to 15/s. error rate for canary nodes: dropped from 9% to 1.2%.

tomas.v: per-request KV footprint distribution shows the heavy tail reduced as expected. the variant with larger KV still presents but fewer sequences per batch so tail impact reduced.

maya.k: ok canary looks good. proceed to 50% then 100% unless we see regression. raj, bump to 50%.

raj.r: `infractl runtime config set --fleet cont-batch-v2 --model redwood/open-13b-q --max_num_seqs 64 --max_batch_tokens 8192 --scope canary=50%` -> rollout started.

deploy-bot: rollout progressed: 50% nodes updated (20/40). no service-level errors reported for updated nodes.

cs-bot: customer updates: AcmeHealth error rate now 1.0% (down from 3.6%), Vaultly 0.5%.

maya.k: good. proceed to 100%. raj?

raj.r: `infractl runtime config set --fleet cont-batch-v2 --model redwood/open-13b-q --max_num_seqs 64 --max_batch_tokens 8192 --scope canary=100%` -> applying to 40/40 nodes.
deploy-bot: rollout complete. all nodes updated.

priya.s: KVCACHE usage trending back to baseline. current total: 52GB. eviction stable. 99p latency back to 210ms, error rate overall 0.6%.

maya.k: great. mitigation looks effective. now actions: 1) maintain override for 48 hours while we run deeper validation 2) create a model profile entry for redwood/open-13b-q-variant that includes the larger per-token KV footprint 3) add a guardrail in runtime that prevents max_num_seqs > 256 for models with KV footprint > X bytes per seq 4) postmortem. anyone take ownership?

tomas.v: I'll own the model profile and validation (item 2). I'll run a suite to compute per-seq KV footprint across our model catalog and tag variants.

raj.r: I'll own the guardrail implementation and the short-term override retention (item 1 and 3). plan: add server-side validation check in deploy pipeline and a runtime enforcement that rejects risky config rollouts, target EOD.

priya.s: I'll own postmortem draft and include timeline + RCA + mitigation + follow-ups. also recommend an alarm on rapid KVCACHE growth delta (e.g., >100GB in 5m) with automatic throttling fallback.

maya.k: good. follow-ups: please file tickets and link here. also need comms for affected customers. @cs-bot can you prepare a templated note we can send to top affected customers explaining impact and mitigation? include apology and invite for any logs.

cs-bot: Draft prepared. Short summary: brief service disruption with elevated latency and errors for redwood/open-13b-q between 09:12 and 09:34 UTC. Root cause: batching config + larger-than-expected KV footprint in new variant causing cache thrash and paging. Mitigation: throttled batching (max_num_seqs lowered) rolled to fleet; full resolution ongoing. Will send to AcmeHealth and Vaultly after approval.

maya.k: approve. send.

cs-bot: Sent to AcmeHealth and Vaultly.

maya.k: final checks before resolving incident: confirm metrics stable for 15m, no new timeouts, and no customer escalations. priya, status?

priya.s: metrics stable for 18m. no new timeouts. tickets opened: INF-4321 (guardrail), INF-4322 (model profile audit), INF-4323 (KVCACHE alarm). postmortem owner assigned to priya.s, incident severity P1 -> downgraded to P2 for tracking.

maya.k: resolving incident now. incident-bot: closing active incident alert for cont-batch-v2 redwood/open-13b-q.

incident-bot: Incident resolved: cont-batch-v2 redwood/open-13b-q. duration: 00:22:00. summary: temporary override reduced max_num_seqs and max_batch_tokens to limit KV pressure; KVCACHE stabilized; errors and latency returned to baseline.

maya.k: postmortem will include timeline, root cause, and recommendations: - enforce model profiling during model onboarding - tighten default batching caps and add per-model caps - auto-throttle when KVCACHE growth exceeds threshold - nightly audit of recent model variants for KV footprint changes

tomas.v: one more note: we'll add a lightweight unit in the model CI that checks KV size delta compared to baseline and fails onboarding if >30% increase without explicit sign-off.

priya.s: adding that to INF-4322.

maya.k: thanks team. great coordinated response. closing thread. :white_check_mark:
